planting.note: Direct sow around the last frost in cool soil; an old cultivar that performs best once summer heat has not yet arrived.

directions: Sow this heirloom pot marigold a quarter inch deep in cool, well-drained soil where it is to grow. Radio is distinguished from most calendula strains by its narrow, rolled, quill-like ray petals in bright tangerine-orange, giving the double blooms a spidery, almost cactus-dahlia texture rather than the flatter form of common cultivars. Deadhead spent flowers regularly to keep new buds coming through the cool season, and expect growth to stall in high summer heat before rebounding as temperatures drop.

common_name: Touch of Red Calendula (Mahogany-Tipped Pot Marigold)

planting.note: Direct sow near the last spring frost; young seedlings shrug off light frost and prefer cool conditions to establish.

directions: Direct sow shallowly in average, well-drained soil in full sun. Touch of Red mixes gold, apricot, and orange semi-double flowers, each ray petal brushed with a streak or edge of brick-red on the reverse and sometimes the face, an effect that shows most vividly when the flowers catch backlight in a border or vase. Pinch or deadhead faded blooms to encourage continuous flowering, and expect a slowdown during peak summer heat with renewed vigor as fall cools the air.

common_name: Alpha Calendula (Tall Double Golden Pot Marigold)

planting.note: Direct sow a few weeks before to just after the last frost; long, sturdy stems make this a favored cut-flower strain for cool-season bouquets.

directions: Direct sow into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun, or start a few weeks early indoors for an earlier first flush. Alpha grows notably taller and stockier than most pot marigold strains, sending up long, straight stems topped with large, fully double, deep golden-orange flowers well suited to cutting gardens and market bouquets. Support with light staking or grow among neighboring plants in windy sites, and harvest or deadhead often to keep stems productive through the cool growing season.

common_name: Prolifera Calendula (Hen and Chickens Pot Marigold)

planting.note: Direct sow around the last frost; the odd branching flower form is a curiosity plant best given a dedicated spot rather than a formal bed.

directions: Sow seed shallowly in ordinary garden soil in full sun. Prolifera, the old 'hen and chickens' calendula, produces a central orange flower ringed by a cluster of smaller offset blooms sprouting directly from the base of the main flower head, an heirloom oddity grown more for conversation-starting novelty than for a tidy floral display. Deadhead the largest heads once they fade to keep the plant producing new clusters, and site it where its unusual habit can be appreciated up close, such as an herb bed or collector's border.

common_name: Orange King Calendula (Classic Double Pot Marigold)

planting.note: Direct sow before or around the last frost in cool soil; one of the oldest garden calendula strains still commonly offered.

directions: Direct sow a quarter inch deep in well-drained soil in full sun. Orange King is a Victorian-era heirloom that set the standard many later calendula strains are still judged against, bearing large, fully double, richly saturated orange flowers on upright, well-branched plants. Deadhead regularly to prevent premature seed set and to stretch the bloom season from spring into the cooler weeks of fall. Its vigor and reliability make it a dependable choice for cutting, edging, or an old-fashioned cottage border.

planting.note: Direct sow as early as the soil can be worked; the taproot resents disturbance, so avoid transplanting.

directions: Press seed lightly into well-drained soil in full sun and keep evenly moist until it germinates. Moody Blues stays notably shorter and more compact than the standard love-in-a-mist strains, forming tidy mounded plants covered in soft sky-blue flowers wrapped in the same threadlike green bracts typical of the species. Its dwarf habit resists flopping in wind or rain, making it useful in containers or front-of-border spots where taller nigella would need support. Let a few seed heads mature and dry for the ornamental inflated pods, and expect reliable self-sowing where it is happy.

subcategory: cut flower and dried seed pod annual

planting.note: Direct sow while the soil is still cool; this species dislikes root disturbance and establishes best from an undisturbed sowing.

directions: Sow directly in well-drained soil in full sun and keep the seedbed lightly moist until seedlings emerge. Exotic bears larger, more open flowers than common love-in-a-mist, sky-blue petals surrounding a dramatic boss of near-black to deep-maroon stamens that give the bloom a striking, almost tropical look despite the plant's cool-season habit. The flowers are followed by large, prominently horned seed pods that dry well for arrangements. Grow it among finer-textured companions so its airy, ferny foliage and architectural pods have room to stand out.
